citation: Carroll, C., Hurry, J., Grima, G., Hooper, A., Dunn, K., & Ahtaridou, E. (2020). Evaluation of Bug Club: a randomised control trial of a whole school primary aged reading programme. The Curriculum Journal, 31(4), 605-625. https://doi.org/10.1002/curj.29
report_number: The Curriculum Journal 31(4):605-625, DOI 10.1002/curj.29; ERIC EJ1276710 (journal article evaluating Pearson's Bug Club). Full-text open-access accepted author manuscript from UCL Discovery (eprint 10105355) and St Mary's University Repository (eprint 3873).
design: Cluster (school-level) randomised control trial in the UK (England + Northern Ireland). 42 schools recruited, matched in 21 pairs on %KS1 Level 2, urban/rural, class size, %FSM and %EAL; pairs randomly allocated to Bug Club vs waiting-list control. After 6 control schools dropped out (with their paired BC schools), the final analysed sample = 15 Bug Club schools vs 15 control schools, with Year 1 and Year 2 pupils (ages ~5-7; registry grade band K-2). Intervention = Bug Club, a Pearson commercial WHOLE-SCHOOL reading programme combining print + ONLINE/DIGITAL reading books (assigned to pupils' online accounts with embedded comprehension/phonics questions reported to the teacher) and Phonics Bug interactive-whiteboard daily phonics lessons; teachers received training in implementation shortly before rollout (this is the 'TPD for digital tools' coding -- teachers trained to deliver a digital reading tool). Control = business-as-usual KS1 English Programmes of Study (England) / Language and Literacy area (NI). In Year 2 the control schools also adopted Bug Club (waiting-list crossover), enabling a within-school replication. Outcome = InCAS computerised, nationally age-standardised reading assessment battery (Reading Standardised + word recognition, word decoding, comprehension, spelling, picture vocabulary subscales). Impact estimated by 2-level (pupil within school) hierarchical regression in Stata, auto-regressing the relevant baseline score and controlling for Pupil Premium, EAL, gender and Year group. Subject = reading/literacy. Immediate post-intervention wave = A1 (July 2015, after two terms of Bug Club). Two-arm (BC vs control).
problems: (1) Test-type coding mismatch with the registry: the meta-analysis supplement codes this study's measure as 'Res/Dev' (researcher/developer-made), but the actual instrument is InCAS (Centre for Evaluation & Monitoring, Durham), a widely-used, nationally age-standardised, computer-adaptive assessment with published national norms (Merrell & Tymms 2007). I have labelled test_type='standardized_independent' per the spec (label by what is actually reported; central filtering decides). Flagging in case the meta-analysts had a different rationale. (2) The accepted-manuscript PDFs (UCL Discovery, St Mary's) place all tables AFTER the references; the UCL AAM saved here (33 pp.) contains the full Table 6 impact table with means, SDs, model coefficients (B), SEs and reported Cohen's d -- so all numbers were obtainable from the legal OA copy (no paywall needed). (3) Two effect-size estimands are available and I report both: the spec-PREFERRED model-based standardized impact (g = J*B/pooled-posttest-SD, where B is the HLM pretest-adjusted impact coefficient from Table 6 at A1) is used as the primary 'g' value; the report's OWN headline 'Cohen's d' column (computed as gain-score difference / pooled SD, NOT pretest-adjusted in the standardizer) is recorded in notes for each row (it is systematically larger, e.g. Reading g(b/s)=0.117 vs reported d=0.18). The meta-analysis most likely used the report's reported Cohen's d. (4) Cluster adjustment: this is a school-randomised cluster RCT. The reported Cohen's d / the B/SD g are derived from pupil-level statistics and do NOT account for clustering, so cluster_adjusted=false; I record n_clusters=30 (15+15) and the reported design ICC for Reading Standardised = 0.13 ('school level variance ... accounted for 13% of the variance on reading standardised', p.13-14) so the value can be cluster-corrected centrally (Hedges 2007). The power-analysis assumed ICC=0.0225 but the OBSERVED reading ICC was 0.13; I use the observed 0.13 for the primary reading measure and leave icc null for subscales where no per-subscale ICC is reported (never guess an ICC). The HLM significance tests DO account for clustering (e.g. Reading A1 B=1.75, SE=0.90, p=.050), but the standardized effect sizes themselves are pupil-level. (5) Multiple waves: I extract the immediate post (A1, two terms, FULL randomised sample) as the main contrasts, plus the A2 wave (three terms, restricted to the Year-1-at-baseline cohort -> is_full_sample handled via notes; this is a longer-treatment subset, not a separate subgroup) for Reading Standardised and word decoding. The A2-to-A3 waiting-list replication (Analysis 3) found NO significant Bug Club effect and is noted but not extracted as TPD-vs-BAU rows because by A3 the 'control' schools had themselves adopted Bug Club (within-school before/after, not a clean concurrent control). The 5-term follow-up (Analysis 4, group A only) has no control comparison (age-equivalent only) and is not extractable as an effect size. (6) Headline finding: small significant positive effect on reading at A1 (es .18), not replicated in Year 2.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Bug Club whole-school reading programme (print + online/digital books + Phonics Bug interactive-whiteboard) vs business-as-usual
effect_sizes.test_name: InCAS Reading Standardised (composite age-standardised reading score)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post / A1 (July 2015, end of two terms of treatment; immediate post-intervention, full randomised sample)
effect_sizes.g_method: Spec-preferred model-based: d = B / pooled posttest SD; B=1.75 (HLM impact coefficient, baseline-reading/PP/EAL/sex/year-adjusted, Table 6, A1 panel), pooled posttest SD = sqrt(((592*15.18^2)+(679*14.78^2))/1271) = 14.968. d=1.75/14.968=0.1169; J(df=1271)=0.99941; g=0.1168. g_se = J*SE_B/SD = 0.99941*0.90/14.968 = 0.0601; g_var=0.003611. Standardised by pooled raw posttest SD. NOTE: report's own headline Cohen's d (gain-score diff / pooled SD) = 0.18 (=> alt g=0.180, var=0.003166, se=0.0563); the meta-analysis may have used 0.18.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 6 (A1 panel), p.28 of UCL AAM; narrative p.13-14
effect_sizes.notes: Report's PRIMARY/headline confirmatory outcome and a COMPOSITE of the word recognition + word decoding + comprehension subscales (also extracted below as subscales). Significant at A1 (p=.050). cluster_adjusted=false (effect-size from pupil-level stats); n_clusters=30, observed reading ICC=0.13 recorded for central Hedges-2007 correction. Reported Cohen's d=0.18.

effect_sizes.test_name: InCAS word recognition subscale (Rasch age-equivalent units)
effect_sizes.notes: Subscale of Reading Standardised composite. Non-significant. icc left null (no per-subscale ICC reported).

effect_sizes.test_name: InCAS word decoding subscale (Rasch age-equivalent units)
effect_sizes.notes: Subscale of Reading Standardised composite; strongest/most consistent Bug Club effect (decoding, attributed to systematic phonics). Significant at A1. icc null (no per-subscale ICC).

effect_sizes.test_name: InCAS reading comprehension subscale (Rasch age-equivalent units)
effect_sizes.notes: Subscale of Reading Standardised composite. Significant at A1. icc null (no per-subscale ICC).

effect_sizes.test_name: InCAS spelling subscale (single-word spelling, Rasch age-equivalent units)
effect_sizes.notes: Spelling -> writing/language => outcome_subject=Other per spec. Separate InCAS scale (not part of the Reading Standardised composite). Significant at A1. icc null.

effect_sizes.test_name: InCAS picture vocabulary subscale (Developed Ability; Rasch age-equivalent units)
effect_sizes.notes: Picture vocabulary (oral/receptive vocabulary, part of InCAS 'Developed Ability') -> language/vocabulary => outcome_subject=Other per spec. Separate scale, not part of Reading Standardised composite. Non-significant at A1. icc null.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Bug Club vs business-as-usual (longer-treatment wave, Year-1-at-baseline cohort only)
effect_sizes.grade_band: K-2 (Year 1 at baseline -> Year 2 at A2)
effect_sizes.timepoint: A2 (Jan 2016, after three terms of treatment; Y1-at-baseline cohort)
effect_sizes.g_method: At A2 the table reports a standardized Beta (.055) and t (2.12), not an unstandardized B, so the spec b/s route is unavailable; g computed from the report's reported Cohen's d (gain-based) = 0.11. g = J(df=629)*0.11; J=0.99881; g=0.1099; Var(d)=(631/(318*313))+0.11^2/(2*631)=0.006350; g_var=J^2*Var(d)=0.006334; g_se=0.0796. (Posttest mean diff / pooled SD = 2.33/15.76 = 0.148; multilevel impact NOT significant after accounting for school variance though Beta t=2.12* at pupil level.)
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 6 (A2 panel), p.29 UCL AAM; narrative p.14
effect_sizes.notes: Secondary/longer-treatment wave restricted to the Year-1-at-baseline cohort (3 terms of Bug Club). is_full_sample=false (only the Y1-at-baseline subset is followed to A2, not the full A1 randomised sample). Reported es=.11. Per narrative, after controlling for school-level variance the Reading Standardised advantage (1.92 std points) was NOT statistically significant at A2. icc=0.13 (observed reading ICC). g from reported Cohen's d.

effect_sizes.g_method: From report's reported Cohen's d (gain-based) = 0.24 (Table 6 A2 panel; standardized Beta=.119, t=3.89***). g=J(df=629)*0.24; J=0.99881; g=0.2397; Var(d)=(631/(318*313))+0.24^2/(2*631)=0.006389; g_var=J^2*Var(d)=0.006370; g_se=0.0798. Posttest diff/pooled SD=0.49/2.020=0.243 (consistent).
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 6 (A2 panel), p.29 UCL AAM; narrative p.14
effect_sizes.notes: Word decoding subscale at A2 (3 terms), Y1-at-baseline cohort only (is_full_sample=false). Significant (p<.001 / Beta t=3.89). Strongest sustained effect (decoding). g from reported Cohen's d. icc null.
